stem: When the two great arteries must be identified in a heart, which finding **establishes** that a great artery is the aorta?

choices.text: It gives rise to the coronary arteries
Its valve lies posterior and to the right of the other semilunar valve
It gives rise to the brachiocephalic arteries
Its valve lies anterior to the other semilunar valve
It gives rise to the pulmonary arterial system

explanation.text: The **aorta** is identified as the vessel of origin of the **brachiocephalic arteries**, which ==never== arise from the pulmonary artery.

explanation.caption: Telling the great arteries apart
head: Feature
Aorta
Pulmonary trunk
rows: Occasionally one, rarely both, connect here

explanation.title: Angiography trap
explanation.text: The brachiocephalic vessels may **opacify with the pulmonary trunk** by filling through a **patent ductus arteriosus**, so telling the two great arteries apart may require careful study.
Coronary origin cannot settle the question: occasionally one, or rarely both, coronary arteries connect to the pulmonary trunk.
Identity of the aorta is established by recognizing it as the vessel of origin of the brachiocephalic arteries, which never arise from the pulmonary artery.

choiceNotes.a: Coronary origin is **not definitive**: occasionally one, or rarely both, coronary arteries may connect to the pulmonary trunk.
choiceNotes.b: This is the **normal** aortic valve position in situs solitus, but identity of the aorta is established by its brachiocephalic branches.
choiceNotes.d: In situs solitus the **pulmonary** valve is normally the anterior one; position does not establish identity.
choiceNotes.e: Giving rise to the pulmonary arterial system defines the **pulmonary trunk**, not the aorta.

stem: In an individual with **visceral and atrial situs solitus**, what is the normal relationship of the two semilunar valves?

choices.text: Pulmonary valve anterior; aortic valve posterior and to the right
Aortic valve anterior; pulmonary valve posterior and to the right
Pulmonary valve posterior; aortic valve anterior and to the left
Aortic valve anterior and to the right; pulmonary valve posterior
Pulmonary valve anterior; aortic valve posterior and to the left

explanation.text: In situs solitus the **pulmonary valve is anterior**, and the **aortic valve is posterior and to the right**.
Fig. 1.15 shows the same idea in section: the curvature of the septum results in the **right ventricular infundibulum** lying **superior and anterior** to the aortic valve.
The pulmonary valve is normally anterior, and the aortic valve posterior and to the right, in individuals with visceral and atrial situs solitus.

choiceNotes.b: Reversed: the **aortic** valve is the posterior one, and it lies to the right.
choiceNotes.c: Reversed: the pulmonary valve is normally **anterior**, and the aortic valve lies to the **right**.
choiceNotes.d: The aortic valve is to the right but **posterior**, not anterior.
choiceNotes.e: The pulmonary valve is anterior, but the aortic valve lies posterior and to the **right**, not the left.

stem: The right and left ventricular septal surfaces are asymmetric. This asymmetry is related **mainly** to which feature?

choices.text: Fibrous continuity between the aortic valve and the anterior mitral leaflet
A more apical septal attachment of the tricuspid valve than of the mitral valve
A moderator band within the right ventricle
An infundibulum present in the right ventricle only
The AV node lying on the right atrial side of the central fibrous body

explanation.text: The two septal surfaces differ **mainly** because only the **right ventricle has an infundibulum**.

explanation.caption: How the two septal surfaces differ
head: Feature
Right ventricular side
Left ventricular side

explanation.text: A minority view (Van Praagh and colleagues) holds that a **small portion** of the subsemilunar conus lies just beneath the **right aortic valve cusp**.
The right and left ventricular septal surfaces are asymmetric, related mainly to presence of an infundibulum in the right ventricle only

choiceNotes.a: True (Fig. 1.14), but it is a feature of the left ventricle, not the stated main cause of septal asymmetry.
choiceNotes.b: This is why the **AV septum** exists; it is not the stated main cause of ventricular septal asymmetry.
choiceNotes.c: The moderator band carries the right bundle branch toward the anterior papillary muscle; it is not given as the cause of asymmetry.
choiceNotes.e: This locates the AV node; it does not explain the asymmetry of the ventricular septal surfaces.

stem: On a transverse section of a normal heart, the sinus part of the ventricular septum is curved. Which description of this curvature is correct?

choices.text: Concave on the right side and convex on the left; accentuated in diastole
Concave on the left side and convex on the right; accentuated in systole
Concave on the right side and convex on the left; accentuated in systole
Concave on the left side and convex on the right; accentuated in diastole
Flat on both sides; unchanged through the cardiac cycle

explanation.text: Higher **left ventricular pressure** makes the sinus septal surface **concave on the left** and **convex on the right**, most marked in **ventricular systole**.

steps.text: **Higher pressure** in the left ventricle
Sinus septal surface **concave on the left**, **convex on the right**
Feature **accentuated** during ventricular **systole**

explanation.text: Fig. 1.15: this curvature of the septum results in the **right ventricular infundibulum** lying **superior and anterior** to the aortic valve.
higher pressure in the left ventricle makes the sinus septal surface concave on the left side and convex on the right (see Fig. 1.15), a feature accentuated during ventricular systole.

choiceNotes.a: Both parts are reversed: the septum is **concave on the left**, and the curvature is accentuated in **systole**.
choiceNotes.c: Right timing, wrong side: higher left ventricular pressure makes the septum **concave on the left**.
choiceNotes.d: Right shape, wrong timing: the curvature is accentuated during **ventricular systole**.
choiceNotes.e: The septum is not flat: higher left ventricular pressure curves it, more so in systole.

stem: Comparing the axes of the right and left ventricular outflow tracts, which statement is correct?

choices.text: Both outflow tracts are almost vertically oriented
The right angles sharply to the right; the left is almost vertical
The left angles sharply to the left; the right is almost vertical
Both outflow tracts angle sharply to the right
The right is almost vertical; the left angles sharply to the right

explanation.text: The **right** ventricular outflow tract is **almost vertical**; the **left** ventricular outflow tract **angles sharply to the right**.

items: Profiled cineangiographically in the **left anterior oblique (LAO)** view
Seen in the **parasternal long axis** view by two-dimensional echocardiography
Fig. 1.16 shows the sharp rightward angulation of the outflow portion of the left ventricular septum; Fig. 1.17: the left ventricular outflow tract is angulated to the right

explanation.text: That of the right ventricle is almost vertically oriented, whereas that of the left ventricle angles sharply to the right (Fig. 1.16)

choiceNotes.a: Only the **right** outflow tract is almost vertical; the left angles sharply to the right.
choiceNotes.b: Reversed: the **left** outflow tract is the one that angles sharply to the right.
choiceNotes.c: The left ventricular outflow tract angles to the **right**, not the left.
choiceNotes.d: The right ventricular outflow tract is **almost vertical**.

stem: **Aortic angulation** describes the orientation of which structures, and how does it change with age?

choices.text: The aortic arch relative to the descending aorta; it decreases with older age
The ventriculoaortic junction and proximal aorta relative to the right ventricular outflow tract; it increases with older age
The ventriculoaortic junction and proximal aorta relative to the long axis of the left ventricle; it increases with older age
The ventriculoaortic junction and proximal aorta relative to the long axis of the left ventricle; it decreases with older age
The pulmonary trunk relative to the ascending aorta; it increases with older age

explanation.text: Aortic angulation = orientation of the **ventriculoaortic junction and proximal aorta** with the **long axis of the left ventricle**; it **increases with older age**.

steps.text: **Older age**
Aortic angulation **increases**
Most extreme form: an almost **horizontal** proximal ascending aorta

explanation.text: The reference axis is the **long axis of the left ventricle**, not the right ventricular outflow tract.
Angulation of the aorta refers to the orientation of the ventriculoaortic junction and proximal aorta with the long axis of the left ventricle.

choiceNotes.a: Wrong structures and wrong direction: the definition uses the ventriculoaortic junction and proximal aorta, and angulation **increases** with age.
choiceNotes.b: The reference is the **long axis of the left ventricle**, not the right ventricular outflow tract.
choiceNotes.d: Right structures, wrong direction: aortic angulation **increases** with older age.
choiceNotes.e: The pulmonary trunk is not part of the definition; it refers to the ventriculoaortic junction and proximal aorta.

stem: A 70-year-old patient with **hypertrophic cardiomyopathy** has marked aortic angulation on imaging. In this disease, increased aortic angulation is associated with which finding?

choices.text: Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
A septum concave toward the right ventricle
A vertically oriented left ventricular outflow tract
Origin of a coronary artery from the pulmonary trunk
A pulmonary valve lying posterior to the aortic valve

explanation.text: In **hypertrophic cardiomyopathy**, increased aortic angulation is associated with **dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction**.

branches.text: Altered flow in the proximal aorta
children: Jet impingement on the aortic wall

explanation.text: In patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, increased aortic angulation is associated with dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction

choiceNotes.b: The septum is **concave on the left** because of higher left ventricular pressure; angulation does not reverse this.
choiceNotes.c: The left ventricular outflow tract normally **angles sharply to the right**; the right one is almost vertical.
choiceNotes.d: A coronary artery occasionally connects to the pulmonary trunk, but this is not linked to aortic angulation.
choiceNotes.e: In situs solitus the pulmonary valve is normally **anterior**; this is unrelated to aortic angulation.

stem: The membranous septum (_pars membranacea_) is the fibrous part of the cardiac septum. It separates the left ventricular outflow tract from which chamber or chambers?

choices.text: The right ventricle only
The right atrium only
The left atrium and the right atrium
The right ventricular infundibulum and the pulmonary trunk
In part the right ventricle and in part the right atrium

explanation.text: The fibrous **membranous septum** separates the **left ventricular outflow tract** from **part of the right ventricle** and **part of the right atrium**.

branches.text: Right ventricular side of tricuspid attachment
Right atrial side of tricuspid attachment

explanation.text: Fig. 1.18 labels the membranous septum as **crossed by the attachment of the tricuspid valve**.
The membranous septum (pars membranacea) is the fibrous part of the cardiac septum separating the left ventricular outflow tract from, in part, the right ventricle and, in part, the right atrium.

choiceNotes.a: Only **part** of it faces the right ventricle (the interventricular component); the rest faces the right atrium.
choiceNotes.b: Only **part** of it faces the right atrium (the membranous AV septum); the rest faces the right ventricle.
choiceNotes.c: The left atrium is not named; the right-sided neighbours are the right ventricle and the right atrium.
choiceNotes.d: The source names the right ventricle and right atrium, not the infundibulum or pulmonary trunk.

stem: The tricuspid valve anulus attaches across the right side of the membranous septum. The part of the membranous septum on the **right atrial** side of this attachment forms which structure?

choices.text: The interventricular component of the membranous septum
The membranous portion of the atrioventricular septum
The muscular portion of the atrioventricular septum
The outlet portion of the ventricular septum
The tendon of Todaro at the central fibrous body

explanation.text: The **tricuspid anulus attachment** splits the membranous septum: the **right atrial** side forms the **membranous portion of the AV septum**.

explanation.caption: Two parts of the membranous septum
head: Side of tricuspid attachment
Faces
Forms

explanation.text: The AV septum has a **superior membranous** portion (this one) and an **inferior muscular** portion.
On the right ventricular side of this attachment is the interventricular component. On the right atrial side, it forms the membranous portion of the AV septum.

choiceNotes.a: The interventricular component lies on the **right ventricular** side of the tricuspid attachment.
choiceNotes.c: The muscular portion is the **inferior** part of the AV septum, not part of the fibrous membranous septum.
choiceNotes.d: Viewed from the left ventricle, it is the **muscular** AV septum that forms part of the outlet septum.
choiceNotes.e: The tendon of Todaro is the continuation of the eustachian valve running to the central fibrous body.

stem: The atrioventricular (AV) septum is the portion of the cardiac septum that lies between which two chambers?

choices.text: Right atrium and right ventricle
Left atrium and left ventricle
Left atrium and right ventricle
Right atrium and left ventricle
Right ventricle and left ventricle

explanation.text: The AV septum lies between the **right atrium** and the **left ventricle** (Fig. 1.17).

children: From the LV side: part of the **outlet septum** (Fig. 1.13)
AV node near the membranous-muscular junction
His bundle passes toward the right trigone between the two parts

explanation.text: It lies between a **right** chamber (atrium) and a **left** chamber (ventricle), not two chambers of the same side.
The AV septum is the portion of the cardiac septum that lies between the right atrium and left ventricle.

choiceNotes.a: The atrial side is right, but the ventricle is the **left** one.
choiceNotes.b: The ventricle is left, but the atrium is the **right** one.
choiceNotes.c: Both sides are reversed: it is the **right** atrium and the **left** ventricle.
choiceNotes.e: The septum between the two ventricles is the ventricular septum.

stem: Which anatomic feature makes the **atrioventricular septum** apparent in the normal heart?

choices.text: The tricuspid septal attachment is more apical than that of the anterior mitral leaflet
The anterior mitral leaflet septal attachment is more apical than that of the tricuspid valve
The anterior mitral leaflet is in fibrous continuity with the aortic valve
The right ventricle alone contains an infundibulum below its semilunar valve
The sinus septal surface is concave on the left and convex on the right

explanation.text: The AV septum exists because the **tricuspid** valve attaches to the septum **more apically** than the **anterior mitral leaflet**.

steps.text: Tricuspid septal attachment sits **more apical**
Anterior mitral leaflet attaches **less apically** on the septum
The septum between the two levels separates the **right atrium** from the **left ventricle** = AV septum
steps.label: gap between the two levels

explanation.text: Fig. 1.18: the **plane of mitral valve attachment** corresponds to the atrial edge of the muscular AV septum and the inferior edge of the membranous septum, but **differs from the plane of the tricuspid valve**. The muscular portion is frequently smaller than depicted.
The AV septum is apparent because the septal attachment of the tricuspid valve is more apical than the septal attachment of the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve

choiceNotes.b: Reversed: the **tricuspid** attachment is the more apical one (Fig. 1.17).
choiceNotes.c: True (Fig. 1.14), but it describes the left ventricular outflow region, not why the AV septum exists.
choiceNotes.d: This is the main reason the two **ventricular septal surfaces** are asymmetric.
choiceNotes.e: This is the septal **curvature** from higher left ventricular pressure, not the basis of the AV septum.

stem: Abnormalities of the conduction system are associated with certain congenital cardiac malformations. Which factors **primarily** determine these abnormalities?

choices.text: The size of the sinus node and the size of the sinus node artery
The degree of aortic angulation and the patient's age
Alignment of atrial and ventricular septal structures and the ventricular architecture
The orientation of myocardial muscle fibers in the right ventricle
The pulmonary artery pressure and the curvature of the septum

explanation.text: Conduction abnormalities in congenital malformations are determined primarily by **alignment between atrial and ventricular septal structures** and the **pattern of ventricular architecture**.
The chapter's description of the conduction system is based on hearts **without** congenital defects.

explanation.title: Where alignment matters
items: The nodal triangle becomes **variable** relative to the coronary sinus when atrial and ventricular septal structures are **malaligned**.
VSDs associated with **malalignment** of portions of the ventricular septum affect the right bundle branch relationships to some extent.

explanation.text: Abnormalities of the conduction system are associated with certain congenital cardiac malformations and determined primarily by the alignment between atrial and ventricular septal structures and the pattern of ventricular architecture

choiceNotes.a: Sinus node size and its artery are described for the normal node, not as determinants of congenital conduction abnormalities.
choiceNotes.b: Aortic angulation is linked to aneurysm, transcatheter valve replacement and LVOT obstruction, not to conduction abnormalities.
choiceNotes.d: Fiber orientation is not named as a determinant; the source names septal alignment and ventricular architecture.
choiceNotes.e: Pressure explains septal curvature; it is not named as the determinant of conduction abnormalities.

source.loc: p. 13, Atrioventricular Node; Bundle of His and Bundle Branches

stem: A surgeon examines the junction between the superior vena cava and the right atrium. Where is the **sinus (sinoatrial) node** normally located?

choices.text: In the muscular AV septum, just anterosuperior to the coronary sinus ostium
At the apex of the triangle of Koch, near the membranous septum
Along the inferior margin of the septal band and the moderator band
Medially, across the crest of the caval-atrial junction, in most hearts
Anterolateral junction of the superior vena cava and the right atrial appendage

explanation.text: The sinus node lies along the **anterolateral** aspect of the junction between the **superior vena cava** and the **right atrial appendage** (Fig. 1.19).

items: **Usual site:** anterolateral SVC-right atrial appendage junction
**Rare variant:** extends **medially** across the crest of the caval-atrial junction
**Depth:** superficial, just beneath the epicardium in the **sulcus terminalis**

explanation.text: Medial extension across the caval-atrial crest is the **rare** case, not the usual position.
The sinus (sinoatrial) node is located along the anterolateral aspect of the junction between the superior vena cava and the right atrial appendage

choiceNotes.a: That is the **AV node**, on the right atrial side of the central fibrous body.
choiceNotes.b: The **AV bundle (His)** is at the apex of the triangle of Koch.
choiceNotes.c: That is the course of the **right bundle branch** in the right ventricle.
choiceNotes.d: Medial extension across the crest occurs only **in rare cases**.

stem: Which description of the **sinus node** is correct?

choices.text: It lies deep in the myocardium and measures about 1 × 3 × 6 mm
It lies just beneath the epicardium in the sulcus terminalis and is pierced by a relatively large artery
It lies within the triangle of Koch, just anterosuperior to the coronary sinus ostium
It lies on the right atrial side of the central fibrous body, against the mitral anulus
It lies at the posteroinferior margin of the membranous septum, about 1 mm in diameter

explanation.text: The sinus node is **superficial** (just beneath the **epicardium** in the **sulcus terminalis**) and is **pierced by the relatively large sinus node artery**.

explanation.caption: Do not mix up the two nodes
head: Feature
Sinus node
AV node
rows: Right atrial side of the central fibrous body (right trigone), anterosuperior to the CS ostium
**Superficial**: beneath the epicardium in the sulcus terminalis
Muscular portion of the AV septum

explanation.text: Its blood supply, the **sinus node artery**, passes **through** the node.
The node is superficial, lying just beneath the epicardial surface in the sulcus terminalis, and is approximately 15 × 5 × 1.5 mm. It is pierced by the relatively large sinus node artery.

choiceNotes.a: Wrong depth and size: the sinus node is **superficial**, and 1 × 3 × 6 mm is the size of the **AV node**.
choiceNotes.c: That describes the **AV node** (triangle of Koch, anterosuperior to the coronary sinus ostium).
choiceNotes.d: That describes the **AV node**, whose left surface lies against the mitral anulus.
choiceNotes.e: That describes the **bundle of His**, about 1 mm in diameter near the central fibrous body.

stem: How does activation spread from the sinus node to the AV node, according to current anatomic and electrophysiologic evidence?

choices.text: Through discrete internodal tracts made of homogeneous specialized cells
Through preferential pathways proven to be formed of Purkinje-type cells
Evenly through the whole atrial wall, with no preferential route
Preferentially through muscle bundles delimited by the right atrial orifices
Through internodal tracts that are well defined anatomically

explanation.text: Activation spreads **preferentially through the muscle bundles delimited by the orifices of the right atrium**; no discrete internodal tracts have been found.

items: **No discrete internodal tracts** of homogeneous cells or fibers have been found
Some have identified **Purkinje-like cells** in the major muscle bundles of adult hearts
**Controversy continues** on whether these pale cells are Purkinje-type cells and whether they form preferential conduction pathways

explanation.text: Fig. 1.19A draws internodal pathways only as **proposed** pathways: they are **not well defined anatomically**.
Investigators have not found discrete internodal tracts composed of homogeneous cells or fibers, although some have identified Purkinje-like cells in the major muscle bundles of adult hearts.

choiceNotes.a: Investigators have **not found** discrete internodal tracts of homogeneous cells or fibers.
choiceNotes.b: Whether the pale cells are Purkinje-type cells forming preferential pathways is still **controversial**, not proven.
choiceNotes.c: Spread is **preferential**, through the muscle bundles delimited by right atrial orifices.
choiceNotes.e: Internodal pathways are **not well defined anatomically** and are shown only as proposed pathways (Fig. 1.19A).

stem: Working through a right atriotomy, a surgeon uses the coronary sinus ostium as a landmark for the AV node. In a normal heart, where does the **AV node** lie?

choices.text: On the left atrial side of the central fibrous body, posteroinferior to the coronary sinus ostium
Superficially in the sulcus terminalis, just beneath the epicardium
On the left ventricular septal surface, beneath the right and noncoronary aortic commissure
At the posteroinferior margin of the membranous ventricular septum
On the right atrial side of the central fibrous body, just anterosuperior to the coronary sinus ostium

explanation.text: The AV node lies on the **right atrial side of the central fibrous body (right trigone)**, in the **muscular AV septum**, just **anterosuperior** to the coronary sinus ostium.

children: Right atrial side of the **right trigone**
Muscular portion of the AV septum
Node is just **anterosuperior** to its ostium
At times its posterior margin lies directly against the ostium
Right trigone lies beneath the nadir of the **noncoronary** cusp

explanation.text: The node is **anterosuperior** to the coronary sinus ostium, not posteroinferior to it.
The AV node lies directly on the right atrial side of the central fibrous body (right trigone) in the muscular portion of the AV septum, just anterosuperior to the ostium of the coronary sinus.

choiceNotes.a: Wrong side and wrong direction: the node is on the **right atrial** side and **anterosuperior** to the ostium.
choiceNotes.b: That is the **sinus node**, superficial in the sulcus terminalis.
choiceNotes.c: This is where the His bundle gives off the **left bundle branch** fibers.
choiceNotes.d: The **bundle of His** reaches the posteroinferior margin of the membranous septum after passing through the right trigone.

stem: Which structure lies directly against the **left** surface of the AV node?

choices.text: The mitral anulus
The tricuspid anulus
The moderator band
The tendon of Todaro
The fossa ovalis

explanation.text: The **left surface** of the AV node lies against the **mitral anulus**.

explanation.caption: Relations of the AV node
head: Direction
Relation
rows: Right atrial side of the central fibrous body (right trigone), muscular AV septum

explanation.text: Shape and size: a **flattened oblong** node, on average **1 × 3 × 6 mm** in adults.
Fig. 1.18: the plane of the mitral valve attachment corresponds to the atrial edge of the muscular AV septum.
It has a flattened oblong shape and an average dimension of 1 × 3 × 6 mm in adults. Its left surface lies against the mitral anulus.

choiceNotes.b: The tricuspid anulus is a boundary of the triangle of Koch, seen from the **right** atrium.
choiceNotes.c: The moderator band lies in the right ventricle and carries the right bundle branch.
choiceNotes.d: The tendon of Todaro is another boundary of the triangle of Koch on the right atrial side.
choiceNotes.e: The fossa ovalis is a separate atrial septal landmark (Fig. 1.20A), not described as touching the node.

stem: Viewed from the right atrium, the AV node lies within the **triangle of Koch**. Which three structures form this triangle?

choices.text: Tricuspid anulus, tendon of Todaro, fossa ovalis
Coronary sinus ostium, fossa ovalis, inferior vena cava orifice
Tricuspid anulus, tendon of Todaro, coronary sinus ostium
Mitral anulus, tendon of Todaro, coronary sinus ostium
Tricuspid anulus, coronary sinus ostium, membranous septum

explanation.text: The triangle of Koch is formed by the **tricuspid anulus**, the **tendon of Todaro** and the **coronary sinus ostium**.

explanation.center: Triangle of Koch (from the right atrium)

children: Runs to the central fibrous body
Usually a good landmark for the nodal triangle

explanation.text: The **fossa ovalis** and the **inferior vena cava** appear nearby in Fig. 1.20A but are **not** boundaries of the triangle.

the AV node can be localized within a triangle—described by Koch (Fig. 1.20)—formed by the tricuspid anulus, tendon of Todaro (continuation of the eustachian valve that runs to the central fibrous body), and coronary sinus ostium.

choiceNotes.a: The fossa ovalis is not a boundary; the third side is the **coronary sinus ostium**.
choiceNotes.b: Only the coronary sinus ostium is a boundary; the fossa ovalis and IVC orifice are not.
choiceNotes.d: Viewed from the right atrium, the boundary is the **tricuspid** anulus; the mitral anulus lies against the node's left surface.
choiceNotes.e: The membranous septum is not a boundary; the third side is the **tendon of Todaro**.

stem: The coronary sinus opening is usually a good landmark for the nodal triangle. In which situation does the position of the nodal triangle relative to the coronary sinus become **variable**?

choices.text: Increased aortic angulation in an elderly patient
A coronary sinus that opens to the left of the ventricular septum
A sinus node artery of relatively large size
A sinus node extending medially across the caval-atrial crest
A right bundle branch that is intramyocardial in its middle portion

explanation.text: With an **abnormal coronary sinus orifice**, such as one opening **to the left of the ventricular septum**, the nodal triangle is variable in relation to the coronary sinus.

items: Coronary sinus opens **to the left of the ventricular septum**
**Malalignment** between atrial and ventricular septal structures

explanation.text: In normal hearts the coronary sinus opening is **usually a good landmark**; it is these abnormal hearts where it can mislead.
but in hearts with an abnormal coronary sinus orifice, the nodal triangle is variable in relation to the coronary sinus.

choiceNotes.a: Aortic angulation is linked to aneurysm, transcatheter valve replacement and LVOT obstruction, not to the nodal triangle.
choiceNotes.c: The sinus node is normally pierced by a relatively large artery; this does not affect the nodal triangle.
choiceNotes.d: This is a rare variant of the sinus node position, not a cause of nodal triangle variability.
choiceNotes.e: This is the usual course of the right bundle branch, not a cause of nodal triangle variability.

topic: Bundle of His and Bundle Branches
stem: The common AV bundle (bundle of His) passes through the right trigone to reach the posteroinferior margin of the membranous ventricular septum. Viewed from the right side, this area lies just inferior to which landmark?

choices.text: The commissure between the tricuspid septal and posterior leaflets
The orifice of the inferior vena cava
The ostium of the coronary sinus
The commissure between the tricuspid septal and anterior leaflets
The base of the anterior papillary muscle

explanation.text: The His bundle reaches the membranous septum **just inferior to the commissure between the tricuspid septal and anterior leaflets** (Fig. 1.19B).

explanation.title: Course of the bundle of His

steps.text: **AV node**
Passes through the **rightward part of the right trigone** of the central fibrous body (about 1 mm wide here)
steps.label: direct continuation

steps.text: Reaches the **posteroinferior margin of the membranous septum**, just below the tricuspid **septal-anterior commissure**
Courses along the **crest of the muscular ventricular septum**, giving off the left bundle branch

explanation.text: This area is just inferior to the commissure between the tricuspid valve's septal and anterior leaflets (see Fig. 1.19B).

choiceNotes.a: The source places this area below the **septal-anterior** commissure, not the septal-posterior one.
choiceNotes.b: The inferior vena cava orifice is not described as a landmark for the His bundle.
choiceNotes.c: The coronary sinus ostium relates to the **AV node**, which lies just anterosuperior to it.
choiceNotes.e: The base of the anterior papillary muscle is where the **right bundle branch** arrives before fanning out.

source.loc: p. 13, Bundle of His and Bundle Branches

topic: Bundle of His and Bundle Branches
stem: Viewed from the left ventricle, the common AV bundle gives off the fibers that form the **left bundle branch**. Beneath which part of the aortic valve does this branching occur?

choices.text: The nadir of the noncoronary (posterior) cusp
The commissure between the left and noncoronary cusps
The commissure between the right and left cusps
The nadir of the right cusp
The commissure between the right and noncoronary cusps

explanation.text: The left bundle fibers branch off **beneath the commissure between the right and noncoronary cusps**, close to the aortic valve, over **6.5 to 20 mm**.

explanation.caption: Conduction tissue seen from the left ventricle (Fig. 1.21)
head: Landmark
Conduction structure
rows: Right trigone, with the **AV node** on its right atrial side
Posteroinferior margin of the membranous septum
Common AV bundle coursing along it
Commissure of the **right and noncoronary** cusps
**Branching** of left bundle fibers (6.5 to 20 mm)
Anteroinferior border of the membranous septum

stem: After arising from the bundle of His near the **anteroinferior margin of the membranous septum**, the right bundle branch runs along the right ventricular septal surface. Which description of its course is correct?

choices.text: Above the medial papillary muscle and along the superior margin of the septal band, to the pulmonary valve
Just below the medial papillary muscle and along the inferior margin of the septal and moderator bands, to the anterior papillary muscle
Along the parietal band and the infundibular septum, to the base of the pulmonary valve
Along the inferior margin of the septal band, ending at the medial papillary muscle without further branching
Across to the left ventricular septal surface, toward the base of the posteromedial papillary muscle

explanation.text: The right bundle passes **just below the medial papillary muscle**, along the **inferior margin of the septal band and moderator band**, to the **base of the anterior papillary muscle**, then fans out.

explanation.text: The His bundle runs along the **posteroinferior** margin of the membranous septum; the right bundle **originates** near its **anteroinferior** margin.

courses along the right ventricular septal surface, passing just below the medial papillary muscle and along the inferior margin of the septal band and the moderator band to the base of the anterior papillary muscle.

choiceNotes.c: The parietal band is the parietal extension of the infundibular septum (Fig. 1.15); it is not on the right bundle's course.
